findings.title: A policy waiver of RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING (or RULE.CIT.DOI / NO_INACCESSIBLE), any target, now crashes scans and fails the QUICK doctor
locations: src/Scan.jl:400 apply_ledger (the new loop over rules_for_scan(id) that throws Ledger.LedgerError)
policy/RULES.toml:95,434,451 (the comments declaring the three waivers refused)
test/scans.jl:187 (the base test that a RULE.CIT.DOI waiver disables the scan, replaced by @test_throws)
findings.after:
for rule in rules_for_scan(id)
        rule == canonical && continue
        e = first(Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy"), 1)
        isempty(e) || throw(Ledger.LedgerError("$rule on $(e[1]["target"]) is a policy waiver of a rule $id enforces but " * ...
findings.why_it_matters: A consumer ledger entry `id = "RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING", scope = "policy", target = "*"` passed CFG.EXEMPTIONS at base and at the released rc.11, and waived that rule's three HTML scans (SCAN.HTML_DOCSTRING_ONCE, SCAN.HTML_PUBLIC_HOME, SCAN.HTML_BASE_LEAK), all of which have it as their canonical `rule`. At head the same entry (1) FAILs CFG.EXEMPTIONS, a QUICK check, so `gbg preflight` exits 2, the makedocs wrapper refuses and TestHarness.gate() errors inside Pkg.test(); (2) makes run_scan throw LedgerError at SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE, outside run_scan's try and uncaught by Main (which catches only ConfigError), so `gbg scan docs` exits 3 as a crash and every scan after it is lost. The same happens for an entry with a narrow target (`target = "docs/src/api/Foo.md"`, a form docs/src/guide/ledger.md documents), which apply_ledger ignored at base and at rc.11. So the rule can no longer be waived in any form: the suggested remedy, `scope = "scan"` on SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE, turns off its canonical RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API as well. The same applies to RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE, whose other surfaces the RULES.toml comment says belong to the panel.
findings.description: The defect the prior audit named was narrow: a target-`*` waiver of a two-rule scan's second rule turned off the whole scan. The fix is much wider. It refuses every policy-scope entry, whatever its target, on any rule that appears second in any scan's check list, and it refuses by throwing from the scan engine instead of a doctor line. That covers RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING, a rule that three other scans own canonically, so a waiver that used to work correctly for those three scans is now rejected. The schema already warns against this failure shape: schema/exemptions.schema.json says of its reason floor that raising it 'crashes Ledger.read, and with it sync, every scan and the docs build, where the doctor would have named the entry and carried on'. The replaced test pinned the base contract; its replacement asserts only the refusal. No test checks that an API_GROUPING waiver still reaches the three HTML scans.
findings.evidence: Ran at head: `unreachable_waiver_scans("RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING") = ["SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE"]`; apply_ledger with pol("RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING", "*") on SCAN.HTML_PUBLIC_HOME -> `(Hit[], 0, true)`; on SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE -> `THROWS GBGCodingTools.Ledger.LedgerError`; with target "docs/src/api/Foo.md" -> `THROWS GBGCodingTools.Ledger.LedgerError`. catalog/scans.toml: `id = "SCAN.HTML_PUBLIC_HOME"\nrule = "RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING"`. src/Scan.jl run_scan: `err isa Ledger.LedgerError && rethrow()` then `kept, exempted, disabled = apply_ledger(...)` outside the try. src/TestHarness.jl:607 `code = GBGCodingTools.doctor(cfg, :QUICK)`; `code == 0 || error(...)`; Doctor.jl:50 QUICK includes "CFG.EXEMPTIONS".

findings.title: Claim checklist narrowed past the version-string defect: about 55% of quantifier items dropped, some genuine claims with them
findings.before:
const CLAIM_QUANTIFIER = r"\b(?:every|never|always|all|none|any|only)\b"i
const CLAIM_TOOL_ID = r"...\.[A-Z_]+\b|\bgbg\s+[a-z]+\b"
...
qu = occursin(CLAIM_QUANTIFIER, s) && occursin(CLAIM_TOOL_ID, s)
findings.after:
const CLAIM_QUANTIFIER = r"\b(?:every|never|always|none)\b"i
const CLAIM_TOOL_ID = r"...\.[A-Z_]+\b|`gbg\s+[a-z]+"
const CLAIM_CLAUSE = r"(?<=[.;!?])\s+|\s+—\s+"
...
qu = any(c -> occursin(CLAIM_QUANTIFIER, c) && occursin(CLAIM_TOOL_ID, c), split(s, CLAIM_CLAUSE))
findings.why_it_matters: Every check-docs lane of every consumer gets this checklist as its mechanical floor, and a lane owes a verdict only on the lines it lists. Base and head regexes run over this tree (src, ext, docs/src, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, policy, instruments, catalog, templates): quantifier-tagged lines fall from 443 to 202. 137 were lost because `all/any/only` were dropped, 96 to the clause split, and 8 because `gbg <verb>` now needs a backtick. Some of the lost lines are real, checkable universal claims about the tool: docs/src/architecture.md "`gbg scan docs --rebaseline prose-shape --reason …` are the ONLY writers.", "`PIN.CONFIG` accepts only `vX.Y.Z`", "`gbg round rerun <round> --lanes …` accepts only lanes `bank`"; src/Scans/ai_banner.jl "SCAN.AI_BANNER — RULE.DOC.AI_BANNER. ... the banner is present on every" (split at the dash); src/CLI/Gate.jl "gate: ROUND.DIR — ... the gate never passes vacuously". The exit class also drops docs/src/guide/verbs.md "The exit contract is one for all: `0`", because `(?<![\w.])[0-3]\s+[a-z]` does not match a backticked code. A seeded quantifier mutation planted on one of these lines no longer reaches any checklist, so a lane's recall is not comparable across the change.
findings.description: The defects cited in the new comment were two: the exit alternative matching the `1` of a version string, and a quantifier anywhere on a line with any verb counting as a claim. The `(?!\.\d)` / `[0-3]\s+[a-z]` guard and the clause split address them. Dropping `only`, `all` and `any` outright, and requiring a backtick before `gbg`, removes a further class of real claims the defects did not involve. The commit message states the measured per-lane reduction ("quantifier items 241→110 in all"), so the change is disclosed rather than silent. It is still an instrument-measurement change wider than the defect that prompted it.
findings.evidence: Measurement script (scratchpad) with the verbatim base and head regexes: `exit: old 205 new 204; quantifier(+tool id): old 443 new 202`; `Dict("bare gbg (no backtick)" => 8, "different clause" => 96, "dropped all/any/only" => 137)`; lost exit sample `docs/src/guide/verbs.md: ... The exit contract is one for all: `0``. Comment at Preflight.jl: "not `all`, `any` or `only`, which ordinary prose is full of".

findings.title: A check-docs round's state-verifier scope now follows check-consistency's latex_source_globs, which can only add
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:590 pass_open state args (inside `if inst in Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS` at Passes.jl:549, so check-docs too)
findings.why_it_matters: Take the PF-shaped config in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1247 (`latex_source_globs = ["src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]`). At base, its check-docs `pass open` sent verify-state `source_scope = [src, ext, docs/src, docs]`. At head it sends six entries, examples/*.jl among them, so every check-docs state verifier prompt and reading scope changes because of a key that belongs to another instrument. Its check-consistency panel went from the two named globs at base to six entries at head. A consumer can no longer narrow the LaTeX-source hat with the key: `latex_source_globs = ["src/*.jl"]` (the CP example at ARCHITECTURE:1359) now changes nothing, since `src` is already present.
findings.description: The defect was that the panel's first reader of the key replaced the four surfaces. Changing the panel to a union answers that, and it returns an unset key to rc.11 behaviour. The same edit also rewires a check-docs code path, pass_open's state verifier for check-docs rounds, to read a check-consistency key. That path had no reported defect: at base and at rc.11 it always sent the four surfaces. The instrument schema's documented meaning of the key was rewritten in the same commit, from 'the consumer's globs when it set any' to 'added to them, never in place of them'.

findings.title: `gbg round scripts` needs --reason, and the schema now rejects records the base verb wrote
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl cmd_round `verb == "scripts" && return refresh_scripts(cfg, round, get(o.values, "reason", ""))`

findings.before:
function refresh_scripts(cfg::AbstractDict, round::AbstractString; io::IO = stdout)
    dir, rec = guard(cfg, round; io)
    dst = Preflight.copy_scripts(cfg, String(rec["instrument"]), round)
    entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))
...
     "required": ["at", "head"]
findings.why_it_matters: `gbg round scripts <round>` exited 0 at base and exits 2 at head. A ROUND.toml holding a `scripts_refreshed` entry the base verb wrote (`{at, head}` only) no longer validates. RoundFiles.read_round throws, Rounds.load turns that into exit 2 for every round verb on the round, RoundFiles.rounds marks the round `:invalid`, and Gate.gate_problems treats `:invalid` as fatal, so `gbg gate`, the makedocs wrapper and TestHarness.gate stop on it. The base verb was never in a release (it postdates rc.11), so only this repository's own rounds could carry such a record. schema_version was not changed.
findings.description: Recording a reason and the replaced shas is a reasonable tightening. But existing records gain three required fields with no migration and no schema_version bump, which breaks reading of any round the previous verb touched. The no-op branch also changes what gets recorded: base appended an entry on every run, head appends nothing when no script differs.

+     "reason",

findings.title: On a root with no git HEAD, `round scripts` replaces scripts and then throws before recording anything
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:413-417 refresh_scripts (install_script inside the loop, HEAD check after it)
src/CLI/Passes.jl:1108 build_fails (UNCHECKABLE refusal of an unreachable or placeholder head)
test/rounds.jl:814 (build no-HEAD tested; refresh no-HEAD untested)
findings.before:
dst = Preflight.copy_scripts(cfg, String(rec["instrument"]), round)
    entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))
    rec["scripts_refreshed"] = push!(...); save(dir, rec)
findings.after:
push!(moved, Dict{String,Any}("name" => name, "from" => old, "to" => sha(new)))
        Preflight.install_script(src, dst)
    end
    ...
    head = Git.head(cfg["root"])
    head === nothing && throw(RoundError("scripts: the root has no git HEAD to record the refresh against"))
findings.why_it_matters: Preflight still opens a round without a HEAD (`head = something(Git.head(root), "0"^40)`, Preflight.jl:952). On such a root, base `gbg round scripts` copied the scripts and recorded the refresh against the zero head. Head overwrites every differing frozen script and only then throws RoundError (exit 2), leaving no `scripts_refreshed` entry. That is the unrecorded mid-round script change the verb's own docstring says it exists to prevent ('doing it by hand is what is not, because it leaves no trace'). `gbg round build` handles the same case in the safe order: it checks HEAD before running anything.
findings.description: Removing the placeholder head was justified: a zero head read as 'nothing changed' in close's staleness diff, and build_fails now refuses that as UNCHECKABLE. The edit applied that decision in the wrong order in refresh_scripts. The HEAD check runs after the side effect, so the refusal no longer protects anything, and nothing records the replacement.
findings.evidence: Current src/CLI/Rounds.jl lines 404 `dir, rec = guard(cfg, round; io)`, 413 `Preflight.install_script(src, dst)`, 417 `head === nothing && throw(RoundError(...))`; guard (Rounds.jl:73-83) checks self verify, CFG.TORN, load and config_sha, never HEAD.

findings.title: AUDIT.GAP: equal base/closed-head strings now WARN when the commit is unreachable
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3 AUDIT.GAP row and §6.8 (contract rewritten from 'equals' to 'or an ancestor of it')
findings.after:
(!isempty(base) && Git.is_ancestor(ctx.root, base, prev)) ||
            push!(gaps, "... is not $(audits[i-1].name)'s closed head ... or an ancestor of it — the commits between were never audited")
findings.why_it_matters: Two closed audits whose `base` equals the previous `closed_head` passed AUDIT.GAP at base and at rc.11 by string comparison. At head the check shells out to `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, which fails when the object is missing: a shallow clone, or history rewritten or garbage-collected after the audit. The same records then WARN and claim 'the commits between were never audited', which is false. An overlapping base, which warned before, now passes; that part is the intended relaxation.
findings.description: The move from equality to an ancestor test is sound, since an overlap leaves no commit unread. The side effect is that a reachability requirement now applies to the equal case too. A cheap string-equality short-circuit before the git call would keep the old verdict for identical shas. This is a WARN only, reported for completeness.
findings.evidence: Git.jl is_ancestor: `return success(pipeline(`git -C $root merge-base --is-ancestor $a $b`; ...))` / `catch; return false`; the new predicate has no `base == prev` short-circuit.
